## Mollie

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/mollie-via-payment-gateway/>

This documentation covers the new payment flow using the **Payment Gateway** field. If you're using the **Payment Gateway** field, continue with this documentation. Otherwise, if you're using the **legacy Payments tab**, your existing payment setup will continue to work without any changes. Please refer to our Legacy Payments documentation .

The new **Payment Gateway** field lets you enable multiple payment options in one place, including Square, PayPal, Mollie, Authorize.Net, Stripe, and Razorpay. This allows users to choose their preferred payment method and pay the amount configured in your form.

For **Mollie payments**, customers can securely complete transactions using credit/debit cards, bank transfers, and other supported local payment methods. When a visitor selects Mollie and submits the form, they are redirected to a secure Mollie checkout page to finish the payment and then returned to your site. All transactions are processed safely through Mollie, allowing you to accept both one-time and recurring payments depending on your setup.

### Installation

- First, you will be required to purchase the **Everest Forms pro** plugin.

- Once your purchase is verified, the plugin zip file will be made available to you on your WPEverest account page.

- Next, download the **Everest form pro** plugin zip from your WPEverest account page

- Then, you will be required to Install the Everest pro plugin through your **WordPress admin dashboard**. To do this, visit **Plugins → Add new → Upload** and and then choose the downloaded zip file, and then install and activate it.

- Now go to Everest Forms > **Addons **> **Payment Gateways** > Mollie.

`For a detailed guide, read our documentation on how to install and activate Everest Forms Pro . `

## Create Mollie API

You will need the Mollie test or live API keys to integrate it to Everest Forms plugin. For this, follow the steps below.

- Log in or sign up to Mollie.

- Go to **More > Developers**

Here, you will find the API keys.

### Integrating Mollie to Everest Forms

- Go to **Everest Forms > Settings > Payments > Payment Method > **Mollie** Settings**.

- Enter the required credentials.

- Click on **Save Changes.**

### Add Mollie to Your Form

Go to **Everest Forms → All Forms** and open the form you want to accept Mollie payments on (or create a new form).

- In the form builder, open **Fields → Payment Fields**.

- Drag the **Payment Gateway** field onto your form.

- Click the **Payment Gateway** field to open its settings on the left.

- In the Gateways section, make sure the Mollie toggle is **turned on**.

#### Add what you’re charging for

Set the price on a **single item**. You can customize it even further by changing its features. Choose between Field to fit your payment forms better

**FieldUse it when…Single Item** You’re selling one product or service at a fixed price
**Single Item (User Defined)** You want visitors to enter their own amount — great for donations
**Multiple Choice** Visitors pick one option from a list (e.g. Small, Medium, Large)
**Checkbox** Visitors can select more than one item at the same time
**Subscription Plan** Visitors choose a recurring billing plan (monthly, yearly, etc.)
**Total** Shows the running total of everything selected — always add this for multi-item forms

### Accepting a One-Time Payment

For a simple payment form — like selling a product or accepting a donation — here’s all you need:

- Add the **Payment Gateway** field and make sure **Mollie **is turned on.

- Add a Single Item field and set your price.

- Add a Total field so visitors can see what they’ll be charged.

- Add an Email field — Stripe needs an email to send the payment receipt.

- After clicking **Save**, copy the generated shortcode and embed it in an existing or newly created page or post.

When a visitor selects Mollie and submits the form, they enter their card details on the form and are charged immediately. You'll see the payment in your Mollie Dashboard and under Everest Forms → Entries.

### Accepting Recurring Payments (Subscriptions)

Use this if you want to charge visitors automatically on a schedule — for example, every month or every year.

The Subscription Plan field lets visitors choose between different plans — for example, Monthly vs Annual.

- For Mollie subscription payments, add the **Payment Gateway** field to the form and ensure that Mollie is enabled.

- Then, in the form builder, go to **Fields → Payment Fields** and drag **Subscription Plan** into your form.

- Click the field to open its settings. By default it has 3 plan options — edit the label and price for each.

- To add more plans click the + button; to remove one click the x button.

- To pre-select a plan, click the circle next to that option.

- To add product images to each plan, turn on Use image choices and upload an image per plan.

### Add a trial period

You can let new subscribers try your service for free before their first charge.

- Click the Subscription Plan field to open its settings.

- Turn on Enable Trial Period.

- Set the length — days, weeks, months, or years.

### Add an expiry date

If your subscription should stop automatically on a specific date, turn on Enable Expiry Date and pick the date from the calendar.

### Send Extra Customer Details to Mollie

By default, Mollie receives the payment amount and email. You can also send the visitor’s first name, Last name, address. This makes it easier to identify payments in your Mollie Dashboard.

- Click on the Payment Gateway.

- Go to **Gateways → **Mollie and click on the accordion.

- Use the dropdowns to match each Mollie field (First Name, Last Name, Address) to the matching field on your form.

- Click **Save**.

### Finishing Up

- Click **Save** in the top right of the form builder.

- Embed the form directly into a page:

- **Existing page** — open the page, paste the shortcode where you want the form to appear, and update the page.

- **New page** — create a new page, paste the shortcode, and publish it.

- Alternatively, copy the shortcode located beside the **Save** button, then add a **Shortcode** block to any page and paste the shortcode into that block.

### How to setup webhook for Mollie

- Your Mollie webhook endpoint URL is:
`https://your-site.com/?everest_forms_mollie_webhook=webhook`

- You do not need to add this URL manually in the Mollie Dashboard. Everest Forms sends it automatically as `webhookUrl` when creating each Mollie payment/subscription.

- Make sure your site is publicly reachable (HTTPS). Local sites need a tunnel like ngrok.

- In WordPress, go to Everest Forms → Settings → Payments and expand Mollie Settings. Enter your Test mode API key and/or Live mode API key.

- Save your settings.

Note: Mollie does not send webhooks for subscription cancel/status changes. Everest Forms syncs those via a scheduled cron job (`everest_forms_mollie_sync_subscriptions`) every 15 minutes.

## How to Use the Payment Gateway Field

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/how-to-use-new-payment-gateway/>

This documentation covers the new payment flow using the **Payment Gateway** field. If you're using the **Payment Gateway** field, continue with this documentation. Otherwise, if you're using the **legacy Payments tab**, your existing payment setup will continue to work without any changes. Please refer to our Legacy Payments documentation .

The Payment Gateway field lets visitors choose how they want to pay — Stripe, PayPal, Square, Authorize.Net, Mollie, or Razorpay — all on the same form. Card fields and redirect messages switch automatically based on what the visitor picks.

Looking for a specific classic gateway guide instead? See PayPal Standard , Stripe , Square , Authorize.Net , Mollie , or Razorpay .

### What’s New?

With **Everest Forms Pro 1.9.17+**, the Payment Gateway field is available under **Fields → Payment Fields** in the form builder.

**One field per form.** Only one Payment Gateway field can be added to a form. Once added, the legacy Credit Card, Square Payment, and Authorize.Net fields are hidden from the field list to prevent duplicate payment UIs.

**Supported gateways:**

Gateway Add-on Checkout type
Stripe Everest Forms Stripe On-page card
PayPal Standard Everest Forms PayPal Standard Redirect to PayPal
Square Everest Forms Square (Pro) On-page card
Authorize.Net Everest Forms Authorize.Net On-page card
Mollie Everest Forms Mollie (Pro) Redirect to Mollie
Razorpay Everest Forms Razorpay Redirect to Razorpay

A gateway appears on the form only when its add-on is active, global credentials are saved, and the gateway is enabled in the field’s Gateways list.

### Installation

- First, you will be required to purchase the **Everest Forms pro** plugin.

- Once your purchase is verified, the plugin zip file will be made available to you on your WPEverest account page.

- Next, download the **Everest form pro** plugin zip as well as the **addons** from your WPEverest account page.

- Then, you will be required to Install the Everest pro plugin and the addons through your **WordPress admin dashboard**. To do this, visit **Plugins → Add new → Upload** and then choose the downloaded zip files. Once the plugins have been **installed**, **activate** them and your addons should be enabled on your website.

### For step-by-step installation help see the install guide

#### Step 1 — Connect Your Payment Accounts

The Payment Gateway field does not replace global payment settings. Each add-on still needs credentials saved once site-wide.
Go to **Everest Forms → Settings → Payments→Payment Method** and fill in the details for each gateway:

Gateway What to enter
Stripe Publishable key and Secret key (Live/Test)
PayPal Standard PayPal email, Mode (Sandbox/Production), Payment type
Square Application ID, Access token, Location ID
Authorize.Net API Login ID and Transaction Key
Mollie API key
Razorpay Key ID and Secret

Also set your **Currency** under the General payments section.

#### Step 2 — Add the Payment Gateway Field to Your Form

- Go to **Everest Forms → All Forms** and open your form or create a new one.

- In the form builder, open **Fields → Payment Fields**.

- Drag **Payment Gateway** onto your form.

- Add your payment fields — Single Item, Multiple Choice, Total, etc.

- Click **Save**.

The field is required by default — visitors must pick a payment method before submitting.

#### Step 3 — Choose Which Gateways to Show

- Click the **Payment Gateway** field to open its settings.

- In **Field Options**, open **Gateways**.

- Toggle each gateway on or off. Drag to reorder them.

- Click the arrow (›) next to any gateway to open its per-gateway settings.

**Good to know:**
1. Gateways without saved credentials appear as disabled until connected globally.
2. PayPal is off by default if no global PayPal email is saved.
3. You need at least one gateway turned on — the form will remind you if all are off.
4. You do not need to enable PayPal or Stripe on the legacy Payments tab when using this field

### Per-Gateway Options

Expand any gateway’s accordion (›) to access settings specific to that provider:

Gateway Options
PayPal Per-form email, Sandbox/Production mode, Cancel URL
Stripe Recurring toggle, iDEAL, map customer fields
Authorize.Net Map Customer Email (required for subscriptions)
Square Subscription options
Mollie Subscription description and recurring defaults

### Payment Fields

Add one or more of these to your form:

Field Use it when…
**Single Item** Selling one thing at a fixed price
**Single Item (User Defined)** Visitor enters their own amount — great for donations
**Single Item (Hidden)** Price is charged silently without showing on the form
**Multiple Choice** Visitor picks one option from a list, each with its own price
**Checkbox** Visitor selects more than one item at the same time
**Quantity** Visitor enters how many of an item they want
**Total** Shows the running total of everything selected

### Accepting a One-Time Payment

- Add the Payment Gateway field and enable Stripe, PayPal, or any combination.

- Add a **Single Item** field and set your price.

- Add a **Total** field so visitors see what they’ll be charged.

- Add contact fields (Name, Email, etc.).

- Click **Save** and embed the form.

What visitors see:
1. Stripe / Square / Authorize.Net — a card entry form appears on the page when they select that gateway.
2. PayPal / Mollie — a redirect message appears and they complete payment on the provider's site.
3. Razorpay — a secure payment popup/modal opens on top of the checkout page, where customers complete payment without leaving the site.

### Accepting Recurring Payments (Subscriptions)

- Add the Payment Gateway field and enable gateways that support subscriptions.

- Add a **Subscription Plan** field and configure plans — price, billing period, trial, and expiry.

- Open each gateway’s accordion (›) and map any required fields (e.g. Authorize.Net requires Customer Email to be mapped).

- Click **Save**.

When both Payment Gateway and Subscription Plan are on the form, Everest Forms automatically treats checkout as subscription mode. You do not need to turn on recurring payments on the legacy Payments tab.

### What Visitors See

- A card grid of payment method logos on the form.

- If only one gateway is enabled it is selected automatically.

- Stripe, Square, Authorize.Net — card input appears inline below the gateway cards.

- PayPal, Mollie, Razorpay — a secure redirect message is shown after submitting.

## RazorPay

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/razorpay-via-payment-gateway/>

This documentation covers the new payment flow using the **Payment Gateway** field. If you're using the **Payment Gateway** field, continue with this documentation. Otherwise, if you're using the **legacy Payments tab**, your existing payment setup will continue to work without any changes. Please refer to our Legacy Payments documentation .

The new **Payment Gateway** field lets you enable multiple payment options in one place, including Stripe, PayPal, Mollie, Authorize.Net, Square, and Razorpay. This allows users to choose their preferred payment method and pay the amount configured in your form.

For **Razorpay payments**, the Everest Forms add-on allows you to seamlessly integrate the Indian payment gateway into your forms. Start taking payments via credit/debit card, net banking, or popular Indian mobile wallets today. Integrate the Everest Forms payment module with Razorpay using this add-on—quickly, securely, and with complete confidence in transaction safety.

### Installation

**Installation** of the Everest form RazorPay addon requires the following steps:

- First, you will be required to purchase the **Everest Forms pro** plugin.

- Once your purchase is verified, the plugin zip file will be made available to you on your WPEverest account page.

- Next, download the **Everest form pro** plugin zip as well as the RazorPay** addon** from your WPEverest account page

- Then, you will be required to Install the Everest pro plugin and the **RazorPay **addon through your **WordPress admin dashboard**. To do this, visit **Plugins → Add new → Upload** and then choose the downloaded zip files. Once the plugins have been **installed**, **activate** them and your addon should be enabled on your website.

`For a detailed guide, read our documentation on how to install and activate Everest Forms Pro . `

## Setup and Configuration

For API Keys:

- Go To ** RazorPay **.

- If you have an account, **log in, **else,** signup.**

- Click on **Settings** on the left-hand side of the screen.

- Click on **API Keys**.

- Click on **Generate Test Key**.

- The **Client Id **and** Secret Key** will appear. Copy these keys and click on** OK**.
**Note: **The Secret Key will only be shown once. Therefore, it is recommended to download the keys.

### Integrating RazorPay API with Everest Forms

To make sure the **RazorPay** addon and the Payments options work perfectly on your website, we suggest you tune its settings to fit your forms better. To open the Payments settings, visit **Everest Forms **→** Settings **through your admin sidebar. Next, click on the **Payments**→ **Payment Method** section inside payments settings.

Once you’ve installed and activated the add-on, you’ll need to enable Razorpay integration within Everest Forms. To complete the setup, you must use your Razorpay account credentials. Follow the steps above to obtain your API keys.

In the Razorpay settings, enter your Publishable Key and Secret Key in the designated fields. If you’d like to test the payment flow before going live, you can use the test keys provided by Razorpay.

To enable testing, simply turn on the **Enable Test Mode** option. In test mode, you can use your Razorpay test credentials to simulate transactions. You can also refer to the official documentation to learn more about test keys and access sample test credit card details for validation.

Hit the **Save Changes **button when you complete the settings

### Add RazorPay to Your Form

Go to **Everest Forms → All Forms** and open the form you want to accept RazorPay payments on (or create a new form).

- In the form builder, open **Fields → Payment Fields**.

- Drag the **Payment Gateway** field onto your form.

- Click the **Payment Gateway** field to open its settings on the left.

- In the Gateways section, make sure the **RazorPay **toggle is **turned on**.

When a visitor selects Razorpay and submits the form, they are redirected to Razorpay to complete the payment. After a successful transaction, they are returned to your site and the payment is logged under Everest Forms → Entries.

#### Add what you’re charging for

Set the price on a **single item**. You can customize it even further by changing its features. Choose between Field to fit your payment forms better

**FieldUse it when…Single Item** You’re selling one product or service at a fixed price
**Single Item (User Defined)** You want visitors to enter their own amount — great for donations
**Multiple Choice** Visitors pick one option from a list (e.g. Small, Medium, Large)
**Checkbox** Visitors can select more than one item at the same time
**Subscription Plan** Visitors choose a recurring billing plan (monthly, yearly, etc.)
**Total** Shows the running total of everything selected — always add this for multi-item forms

### Accepting a One-Time Payment

For a simple payment form — like selling a product or accepting a donation — here’s all you need:

- Add the **Payment Gateway** field and make sure **RazorPay** is turned on.

- Add a Single Item field and set your price.

- Add a Total field so visitors can see what they’ll be charged.

- Add an Email field — RazorPay needs an email to send the payment receipt.

- After clicking **Save**, copy the generated shortcode and embed it in an existing or newly created page or post.

When a visitor selects RazorPay and submits the form, they enter their card details on the form and are charged immediately. You'll see the payment in your RazorPay Dashboard and under Everest Forms → Entries.

### Accepting Recurring Payments (Subscriptions)

Use this if you want to charge visitors automatically on a schedule — for example, every month or every year.

The Subscription Plan field lets visitors choose between different plans — for example, Monthly vs Annual.

- For RazorPay subscription payments, add the **Payment Gateway** field to the form and ensure that **RazorPay** is enabled.

- Then, in the form builder, go to **Fields → Payment Fields** and drag **Subscription Plan** into your form.

- Click the field to open its settings. By default it has 3 plan options — edit the label and price for each.

- To add more plans click the + button; to remove one click the x button.

- To pre-select a plan, click the circle next to that option.

- To add product images to each plan, turn on Use image choices and upload an image per plan.

### Add a trial period

You can let new subscribers try your service for free before their first charge.

- Click the Subscription Plan field to open its settings.

- Turn on Enable Trial Period.

- Set the length — days, weeks, months, or years.

### Add an expiry date

If your subscription should stop automatically on a specific date, turn on Enable Expiry Date and pick the date from the calendar.

### Finishing Up

- Click **Save** in the top right of the form builder.

- Embed the form directly into a page:

- **Existing page** — open the page, paste the shortcode where you want the form to appear, and update the page.

- **New page** — create a new page, paste the shortcode, and publish it.

- Alternatively, copy the shortcode located beside the **Save** button, then add a **Shortcode** block to any page and paste the shortcode into that block.

### How to setup webhook for Razorpay

- Copy your Razorpay webhook endpoint URL:
`https://your-site.com/?evf-razorpay-webhook=1`

- Log in to your Razorpay Dashboard and go to Account & Settings → Webhooks (or Developers → Webhooks).

- Click Add New Webhook and paste the URL above into the Webhook URL field.

- Under Active Events, select these events, then click Create Webhook:

- `payment.captured`

- `payment.failed`

- `payment.refunded`

- `order.paid`

- `refund.processed`

- `subscription.authenticated`

- `subscription.activated`

- `subscription.charged`

- `subscription.pending`

- `subscription.halted`

- `subscription.cancelled`

- `subscription.completed`

- `subscription.paused`

- `subscription.resumed`

- Razorpay shows a Webhook Secret. Copy it.

- In WordPress, go to Everest Forms → Settings → Payments and expand Razorpay Settings. Paste the secret into Live Webhook Secret (or Test Webhook Secret if you’re in test mode).

- Save your settings.

## Authorize.Net

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/authorize-via-payment-gateway/>

This documentation covers the new payment flow using the **Payment Gateway** field. If you're using the **Payment Gateway** field, continue with this documentation. Otherwise, if you're using the **legacy Payments tab**, your existing payment setup will continue to work without any changes. Please refer to our Legacy Payments documentation .

The new **Payment Gateway** field lets you enable multiple payment options in one place, including Authorize, PayPal, Mollie, Stripe, Square, and Razorpay. This allows users to choose their preferred payment method and pay the amount configured in your form.

If you want to accept payments securely on your website, the **Authorize.Net add-on** for Everest Forms is a reliable solution. It allows your users to pay directly on your forms using credit cards without being redirected away from your site. It supports both one-time payments and recurring subscriptions, making it a flexible option for managing online transactions.

### Installation

**Installation** of the Everest form Authorize.net addon requires the following steps:

- First, you will be required to purchase the **Everest Forms pro** plugin.

- Once your purchase is verified, the plugin zip file will be made available to you on your WPEverest account page.

- Next, download the **Everest form pro** plugin zip as well as the Authorize.net **addon** from your WPEverest account page

- Then, you will be required to Install the Everest pro plugin and the Authorize.net addon through your **WordPress admin dashboard**. To do this, visit **Plugins → Add new → Upload** and then choose the downloaded zip files. Once the plugins have been **installed**, **activate** them and your addon should be enabled on your website.

`For a detailed guide, read our documentation on how to install and activate Everest Forms Pro . `

### Getting API Keys

You can use either Live or Test APIs with the Authorize.net payment system. To generate the API, follow the steps below.

- Sign In to the Authorize.net account .

- If you don’t have an account, create one .

- Once you are logged in, you will see a popup from which you can toggle between live or test mode.

- You can remove the popup from the available buttons and then go to** Account > Settings**.

- Inside Settings, click on **API Credentials & Keys**. Here, you will find the necessary keys.

- You will need an API Login ID and a Transaction key. When you create an account, you will be given with both of these keys in the beginning.

In this tutorial, we assume that you have to create a new transaction key. For this, you can click on the ‘**New Transaction Key**‘ option and click on **Submit.**

In this tutorial, we assume that you have to create a new transaction key. For this, you can click on the ‘**New Transaction Key**‘ option and click on **Submit.**

After clicking on the submit button, the app will require you to put the verification key sent to your email. You can request this key by clicking on the ‘Request Pin’ button on the pop-up.

Once you’ve verified your identity, Authorize.Net will display your Transaction Key. Click the Copy to Clipboard button.

Now, after copying both the API login key and the Transaction Key, you can now connect the Everest Forms with the Authorize.net payment portal.

### Setup and Configuration

To make sure the Authorize.net addon and the Payments options work perfectly on your website, we suggest you tune its settings to fit your forms better. To open the Payments settings, visit **Everest Forms **→** Settings **through your admin sidebar. Next, click on the **Payments**→ **Payment Method** section inside payments settings.

### Add Authorize.net to Your Form

Go to **Everest Forms → All Forms** and open the form you want to accept Authorize.net payments on (or create a new form).

- In the form builder, open **Fields → Payment Fields**.

- Drag the **Payment Gateway** field onto your form.

- Click the **Payment Gateway** field to open its settings on the left.

- In the Gateways section, make sure the **Authorize.net** toggle is **turned on**.

When a visitor selects Authorize.net on your form, a card entry box appears automatically — no extra setup needed.

#### Add what you’re charging for

Set the price on a **single item**. You can customize it even further by changing its features. Choose between Field to fit your payment forms better

**FieldUse it when…Single Item** You’re selling one product or service at a fixed price
**Single Item (User Defined)** You want visitors to enter their own amount — great for donations
**Multiple Choice** Visitors pick one option from a list (e.g. Small, Medium, Large)
**Checkbox** Visitors can select more than one item at the same time
**Subscription Plan** Visitors choose a recurring billing plan (monthly, yearly, etc.)
**Total** Shows the running total of everything selected — always add this for multi-item forms

### Accepting a One-Time Payment

For a simple payment form — like selling a product or accepting a donation — here’s all you need:

- Add the **Payment Gateway** field and make sure **Authorize.net** is turned on.

- Add a Single Item field and set your price.

- Add a Total field so visitors can see what they’ll be charged.

- Add an Email field — Authorize.net needs an email to send the payment receipt.

- After clicking **Save**, copy the generated shortcode and embed it in an existing or newly created page or post.

When a visitor selects Authorize.net and submits the form, they enter their card details on the form and are charged immediately. You'll see the payment in your Authorize.net Dashboard and under Everest Forms → Entries.

### Accepting Recurring Payments (Subscriptions)

Use this if you want to charge visitors automatically on a schedule — for example, every month or every year.

The Subscription Plan field lets visitors choose between different plans — for example, Monthly vs Annual.

- For Authorize.net subscription payments, add the **Payment Gateway** field to the form and ensure that **Authorize.net** is enabled.

- Use the dropdowns to map **Authorize.Net** fields to your form. **Email is required**, while other fields like Payment Description, First Name, Last Name, Company Name, and Billing Address are optional.

- Then, in the form builder, go to **Fields → Payment Fields** and drag **Subscription Plan** into your form.

- Click the field to open its settings. By default it has 3 plan options — edit the label and price for each.

- To add more plans click the + button; to remove one click the x button.

- To pre-select a plan, click the circle next to that option.

- To add product images to each plan, turn on Use image choices and upload an image per plan.

### Add a trial period

You can let new subscribers try your service for free before their first charge.

- Click the Subscription Plan field to open its settings.

- Turn on Enable Trial Period.

- Set the length — days, weeks, months, or years.

### Add an expiry date

If your subscription should stop automatically on a specific date, turn on Enable Expiry Date and pick the date from the calendar.

### Send Extra Customer Details to Authorize.net

By default, Authorize.net receives the payment amount and email. You can also send the visitor’s name, phone number, address, and a transaction description. This makes it easier to identify payments in your Authorize.net Dashboard.

- Click on the Payment Gateway

- Go to **Gateways → Authorize.net** and click on the accordion.

- Use the dropdowns to match each Authorize.net field (Payment Description, Payment Recepit Mail, Email Subscriptions , First Name, Last Name, Company Name, Billing Address) to the matching field on your form.

- Click Save.

### Finishing Up

- Click **Save** in the top right of the form builder.

- Embed the form directly into a page:

- **Existing page** — open the page, paste the shortcode where you want the form to appear, and update the page.

- **New page** — create a new page, paste the shortcode, and publish it.

- Alternatively, copy the shortcode located beside the **Save** button, then add a **Shortcode** block to any page and paste the shortcode into that block.

### How to setup webhook for AUthorize.Net

- Copy your Authorize.Net webhook endpoint URL:`https://your-site.com/?evf-authorize-net-webhook=1`

- Log in to the **Authorize.Net Merchant Interface** and go to **Account → Business Settings → Webhooks**.

- Click **Add Endpoint**, give it a name, and paste the URL above into the **Endpoint URL** field.

- Set **Status** to **Active**, select the events below, and save.

- Copy the **Signature Key** from **Account → Settings → API Credentials & Keys** (or from the webhook screen).

- In WordPress, go to **Everest Forms → Settings → Payments → Payment Method** and expand **Authorize.Net Settings**. Paste the key into the **Live Webhook Signature Key** field (or **Test Webhook Signature Key** for the sandbox).

- Save your settings.

Note: Webhooks are rejected until the Signature Key is saved in Everest Forms, so this step is required — not optional. Use the sandbox key while Test Mode is enabled.

## Square

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/square-via-payment-gateway/>

This documentation covers the new payment flow using the **Payment Gateway** field. If you're using the **Payment Gateway** field, continue with this documentation. Otherwise, if you're using the **legacy Payments tab**, your existing payment setup will continue to work without any changes. Please refer to our Legacy Payments documentation .

The new **Payment Gateway** field lets you enable multiple payment options in one place, including Square, PayPal, Mollie, Authorize.Net, Stripe, and Razorpay. This allows users to choose their preferred payment method and pay the amount configured in your form.

For Square payments, the **Square** allows you to accept credit and debit card payments directly on your forms. Customers can enter their payment details securely without leaving your site, and transactions are processed through Square. You can collect one-time payments or set up one-time and recurring payments depending on your setup.

### Installation

- First, you will be required to purchase the **Everest Forms pro** plugin.

- Once your purchase is verified, the plugin zip file will be made available to you on your WPEverest account page.

- Next, download the **Everest form pro** plugin zip from your WPEverest account page

- Then, you will be required to Install the Everest pro plugin through your **WordPress admin dashboard**. To do this, visit **Plugins → Add new → Upload** and and then choose the downloaded zip file, and then install and activate it.

- Now go to Everest Forms > **Addons **> **Payment Gateways** > **Square**.

`For a detailed guide, read our documentation on how to install and activate Everest Forms Pro . `

## Configuration Sqaure

To integrate Square with the Everest Forms, you will need to have an Application ID, Access Token, and Location ID from your Square account.

### Generating an Application ID, Access Token, and Location ID

- Go to https://developer.squareup.com .

- Log in or sign up to a developer account.

- Open an application. If you don’t have an application, you can create one on the **Applications page**.

- In the left pane, choose **Credentials**.

- To get your **ProductionAccess token and Application ID**:

- At the top of the page, choose **Production**

- .In the **Production Access token** box, choose **Show** and copy your token.

- To get your **Sandbox Access token and Application ID**:

- At the top of the page, choose **Sandbox**.

- In the **Sandbox Access token** box, choose **Show** and copy your token.

- To get your **Location ID**:

- In the left panel, go to Locations.

- Here, you can find the Location ID for the Sandbox and Production modes.

### Integrating Square to Everest Forms

- Go to **Everest Forms > Settings > Payments > Payment Method > Square Settings**.

- Enter the required credentials.

- Click on **Save Changes.**

### Add Square to Your Form

Go to **Everest Forms → All Forms** and open the form you want to accept Square payments on (or create a new form).

- In the form builder, open **Fields → Payment Fields**.

- Drag the **Payment Gateway** field onto your form.

- Click the **Payment Gateway** field to open its settings on the left.

- In the Gateways section, make sure the **Square** toggle is **turned on**.

When a visitor selects Square on your form, a card entry box appears automatically — no extra setup needed.

#### Add what you’re charging for

Set the price on a **single item**. You can customize it even further by changing its features. Choose between Field to fit your payment forms better

**FieldUse it when…Single Item** You’re selling one product or service at a fixed price
**Single Item (User Defined)** You want visitors to enter their own amount — great for donations
**Multiple Choice** Visitors pick one option from a list (e.g. Small, Medium, Large)
**Checkbox** Visitors can select more than one item at the same time
**Subscription Plan** Visitors choose a recurring billing plan (monthly, yearly, etc.)
**Total** Shows the running total of everything selected — always add this for multi-item forms

### Accepting a One-Time Payment

For a simple payment form — like selling a product or accepting a donation — here’s all you need:

- Add the **Payment Gateway** field and make sure **Square **is turned on.

- Add a Single Item field and set your price.

- Add a Total field so visitors can see what they’ll be charged.

- Add an Email field — Stripe needs an email to send the payment receipt.

- After clicking **Save**, copy the generated shortcode and embed it in an existing or newly created page or post.

When a visitor selects Square and submits the form, they enter their card details on the form and are charged immediately. You'll see the payment in your Square Dashboard and under Everest Forms → Entries.

### Accepting Recurring Payments (Subscriptions)

Use this if you want to charge visitors automatically on a schedule — for example, every month or every year.

The Subscription Plan field lets visitors choose between different plans — for example, Monthly vs Annual.

- For Square subscription payments, add the **Payment Gateway** field to the form and ensure that Square is enabled.

- Then, in the form builder, go to **Fields → Payment Fields** and drag **Subscription Plan** into your form.

- Click the field to open its settings. By default it has 3 plan options — edit the label and price for each.

- To add more plans click the + button; to remove one click the x button.

- To pre-select a plan, click the circle next to that option.

- To add product images to each plan, turn on Use image choices and upload an image per plan.

### Add a trial period

You can let new subscribers try your service for free before their first charge.

- Click the Subscription Plan field to open its settings.

- Turn on Enable Trial Period.

- Set the length — days, weeks, months, or years.

### Add an expiry date

If your subscription should stop automatically on a specific date, turn on Enable Expiry Date and pick the date from the calendar.

### Send Extra Customer Details to Square

By default, Square receives the payment amount and email. You can also send the visitor’s first name, Last name, address. This makes it easier to identify payments in your Square Dashboard.

- Click on the Payment Gateway.

- Go to **Gateways → Square** and click on the accordion.

- Use the dropdowns to match each Square field (First Name, Last Name, Address) to the matching field on your form.

- Click **Save**.

### Finishing Up

- Click **Save** in the top right of the form builder.

- Embed the form directly into a page:

- **Existing page** — open the page, paste the shortcode where you want the form to appear, and update the page.

- **New page** — create a new page, paste the shortcode, and publish it.

- Alternatively, copy the shortcode located beside the **Save** button, then add a **Shortcode** block to any page and paste the shortcode into that block.

### How to setup webhook for Square

- Copy your Square webhook endpoint URL:
`https://your-site.com/?evf-square-webhook=1`

- Log in to the Square Developer Dashboard , open your application, and go to Webhooks.

- Click Add Endpoint and paste the URL above into the Notification URL field.

- Subscribe to these event types, then save:

- `payment.created`

- `payment.updated`

- `subscription.created`

- `subscription.updated`

- Square generates a Signature Key. Copy it.

- In WordPress, go to Everest Forms → Settings → Payments and expand Square Settings. Paste the key into Live Webhook Signature Key (or Test Webhook Signature Key if you’re in test mode).

- Save your settings.

Note: Square uses separate credentials and signature keys for Sandbox and Production. Match the signature key to the mode set by Enable Test Mode in Square Settings.

## PayPal Standard

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/paypal-via-payment-gateway/>

This documentation covers the new payment flow using the **Payment Gateway** field. If you're using the **Payment Gateway** field, continue with this documentation. Otherwise, if you're using the **legacy Payments tab**, your existing payment setup will continue to work without any changes. Please refer to our Legacy Payments documentation .

The new **Payment Gateway** field lets you enable multiple payment options in one place, including Paypal, Stripe, Mollie, Authorize.Net, Square, and Razorpay. This allows users to choose their preferred payment method and pay the amount configured in your form.

For PayPal payments, the **PayPal Standard** addon lets visitors pay using their PayPal account directly from your form. After submission, they are redirected to PayPal to complete the payment securely and then returned to your site. You can collect one-time payments or set up recurring subscriptions.

### Installation

**Installation** of the Everest form PayPal addon requires the following steps:

- First, you will be required to purchase the **Everest Forms pro** plugin.

- Once your purchase is verified, the plugin zip file will be made available to you on your WPEverest account page.

- Next, download the **Everest form pro** plugin zip as well as the **PayPal Standard addon** from your WPEverest account page

- Then, you will be required to Install the Everest form pro plugin and the PayPal addon through your **WordPress admin dashboard**. To do this, visit **Plugins → Add new → Upload** and then choose the downloaded zip files. Once the plugins have been **installed**, **activate** them and your addon should be enabled on your website.

`For a detailed guide, read our documentation on how to install and activate Everest Forms Pro . `

### PayPal Global Settings

The **Global PayPal Settings** allow you to configure PayPal parameters once and apply them to all forms, eliminating the need to set up PayPal credentials for each form. After you enable the Paypal addon, you can click on the settings icon to access the settings:

Else, navigate to the global PayPal configuration through your WordPress admin:

Configure PayPal Settings through Global Payments Settings

You can now configure the global settings for PayPal from here:

Under the **PayPal Settings**, configure all the details related to your PayPal account:

- **PayPal Email Address: **Enter your primary PayPal business account email. This email will receive all payment notifications across your site and must be registered with PayPal.

- **Mode: **Choose between **Production and Sandbox mode**.
Production mode is used for live transactions involving real money, while sandbox mode is used for testing and development purposes.

- **Payment Type:** Choose between Product & Service and Donation Payments.
Product & Service is suitable for selling products, services, or digital downloads and provides a standard **PayPal** checkout experience. On the other hand, **Donation Payment** is optimized for charitable organizations and fundraising.

- **Cancel URL: **Define the location to which users are redirected if they cancel the PayPal payment. So add the URL to your homepage, customer support, or anything that you feel is suitable.

Click on the **Save Changes **once you have completed configuring global settings for PayPal.

### Add PayPal to Your Form

Go to **Everest Forms → All Forms** and open the form you want to accept PayPal payments on, or create a new one.

- In the form builder, open **Fields → Payment Fields**.

- Drag the **Payment Gateway** field onto your form.

- Click the **Payment Gateway** field to open its settings on the left.

- In the Gateways section, make sure the **PayPal **toggle is **turned on**.

- To use the **Paypal Global Settings** enable the **Use Global PayPal SettingsAlternatively**, if you need different settings for a specific form—for example, a different PayPal email address or cancel URL—you can override the global settings for that form from the **Payment Gateway** section.

Note: For PayPal to appear in both the Form Builder and on the frontend, either enable Use **Global PayPal Settings** or configure the **PayPal settings** for the form under Payment Gateway → PayPal. After enabling PayPal, complete the required PayPal settings fields.

### Add what you’re charging for

Set the price on a **single item**. You can customize it even further by changing its features. Choose between Field to fit your payment forms better

**FieldUse it when…Single Item** You’re selling one product or service at a fixed price
**Single Item (User Defined)** You want visitors to enter their own amount — great for donations
**Multiple Choice** Visitors pick one option from a list (e.g. Small, Medium, Large)
**Checkbox** Visitors can select more than one item at the same time
**Subscription Plan** Visitors choose a recurring billing plan (monthly, yearly, etc.)
**Total** Shows the running total of everything selected — always add this for multi-item forms

### Accepting a One-Time Payment

For a simple payment form — like selling a product or accepting a donation — here’s all you need:

- Add the **Payment Gateway** field to your form and ensure that **PayPal** is enabled. Also, make sure the PayPal configuration requirements mentioned above have been completed.

- Add a Single Item field and set your price.

- Click Save, then copy the shortcode and paste it on any page or post.

When a visitor selects PayPal and submits, they are redirected to PayPal to pay and then returned to your site. The payment appears under Everest Forms → Entries.

### Accepting Recurring Payments (Subscriptions)

Use this if you want to charge visitors automatically on a schedule — for example, every month or every year.

The Subscription Plan field lets visitors choose between different plans — for example, Monthly vs Annual.

- For PayPal subscription payments, add the **Payment Gateway** field to the form and ensure that **PayPal** is enabled.

- Then, in the form builder, go to **Fields → Payment Fields** and drag **Subscription Plan** into your form.

- Click the field to open its settings. By default it has 3 plan options — edit the label and price for each.

- To add more plans click the + button; to remove one click the x button.

- To pre-select a plan, click the circle next to that option.

- To add product images to each plan, turn on Use image choices and upload an image per plan.

### Add a trial period

You can let new subscribers try your service for free before their first charge.

- Click the Subscription Plan field to open its settings.

- Turn on Enable Trial Period.

- Set the length — days, weeks, months, or years.

### Add an expiry date

If your subscription should stop automatically on a specific date, turn on Enable Expiry Date and pick the date from the calendar.

### Finishing Up

- Click **Save** in the top right of the form builder.

- Embed the form directly into a page:

- **Existing page** — open the page, paste the shortcode where you want the form to appear, and update the page.

- **New page** — create a new page, paste the shortcode, and publish it.

- Alternatively, copy the shortcode located beside the **Save** button, then add a **Shortcode** block to any page and paste the shortcode into that block.

### How to setup IPN for PayPal

- Copy your PayPal IPN endpoint URL:
`https://your-site.com/index.php?evf-listener=IPN`

- Log in to your live PayPal business account at paypal.com (not sandbox).

- Go to Account Settings → Notifications → Instant payment notifications.

- Click Update, turn IPN on, and paste the URL above into the Notification URL field.

- Enable message delivery and save.

- In WordPress, go to Everest Forms → Settings → Payments and expand Paypal Settings.

- Enter your live Paypal Email Address.

- Set mode to Production.

- Save your settings.

## Stripe

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/stripe-via-payment-gateway/>

This documentation covers the new payment flow using the **Payment Gateway** field. If you're using the **Payment Gateway** field, continue with this documentation. Otherwise, if you're using the **legacy Payments tab**, your existing payment setup will continue to work without any changes. Please refer to our Legacy Payments documentation .

The new **Payment Gateway** field lets you enable multiple payment options in one place, including Stripe, PayPal, Mollie, Authorize.Net, Square, and Razorpay. This allows users to choose their preferred payment method and pay the amount configured in your form.

For Stripe payments, the **Stripe add-on** lets you accept credit and debit card payments directly on your forms. Visitors can enter their card details without leaving your site, and payments are processed securely through Stripe. You can collect one-time payments or set up recurring subscriptions.

### Installation

**Installation** of the Everest form stripe addon requires the following steps:

- First, you will be required to purchase the **Everest Forms pro** plugin.

- Once your purchase is verified, the plugin zip file will be made available to you on your WPEverest account page.

- Next, download the **Everest form pro** plugin zip as well as the **Stripe addon** from your WPEverest account page

- Then, you will be required to Install the Everest pro plugin and the Stripe addon through your **WordPress admin dashboard**. To do this, visit **Plugins → Add new → Upload** and then choose the downloaded zip files. Once the plugins have been **installed**, **activate** them and your addon should be enabled on your website.

`For a detailed guide, read our documentation on how to install and activate Everest Forms Pro . `

### Connect Stripe

To make sure the Stripe addon and the Payments options work perfectly on your website, we suggest you tune its settings to fit your forms better. To open the Payments settings, visit **Everest Forms **→** Settings **through your admin sidebar. Next, click on the **Payments**→ **Payment Method** section inside payments settings.

Once you’ve installed the addon and activated it, you will be required to activate Stripe’s features on Everest form. To proceed with the Stripe setup, you will be required to use your Stripe account’s API keys. To retrieve your **API keys**, follow these simple steps:

- Open your **Stripe Dashboard.**

- Visit the **API keys** page by clicking under **API keys** under the **Developer** tab on the dashboard sidebar. (**Developer → API keys.**)

- Create and copy your **API keys** through this page. To learn more about the process involved in using API keys, you can refer to this page on the Stripe website.

Next, you can change **various settings** for Stripe to make it fit better for your website.

Now, return to your WordPress dashboard and navigate to **Everest Forms >Settings >Payments>Payment Method**.

Under Stripe settings, you can insert the **Publishable key** and the **Secret key** to the appropriate fields. If you want to test the payment system before going live, use the Test keys that you may have received for the **Stripe API.**

If you want to test the payment system before going live, click on the **Enable Test mode** option. For the test mode, you can use the Test keys that you may have received for the Stripe API. You can learn more about the Test keys and receive Test credit cards by referring to this page .

Hit the **Save Changes **button when you complete the settings

### Add Stripe to Your Form

Go to **Everest Forms → All Forms** and open the form you want to accept Stripe payments on (or create a new form).

- In the form builder, open **Fields → Payment Fields**.

- Drag the **Payment Gateway** field onto your form.

- Click the **Payment Gateway** field to open its settings on the left.

- In the Gateways section, make sure the **Stripe **toggle is **turned on**.

When a visitor selects Stripe on your form, a card entry box appears automatically — no extra setup needed.

#### Add what you’re charging for

Set the price on a **single item**. You can customize it even further by changing its features. Choose between Field to fit your payment forms better

**FieldUse it when…Single Item** You’re selling one product or service at a fixed price
**Single Item (User Defined)** You want visitors to enter their own amount — great for donations
**Multiple Choice** Visitors pick one option from a list (e.g. Small, Medium, Large)
**Checkbox** Visitors can select more than one item at the same time
**Subscription Plan** Visitors choose a recurring billing plan (monthly, yearly, etc.)
**Total** Shows the running total of everything selected — always add this for multi-item forms

### Accepting a One-Time Payment

When a visitor selects Stripe and submits the form, they enter their card details on the form and are charged immediately. You'll see the payment in your Stripe Dashboard and under Everest Forms → Entries.

### Accepting Recurring Payments (Subscriptions)

Use this if you want to charge visitors automatically on a schedule — for example, every month or every year.

The Subscription Plan field lets visitors choose between different plans — for example, Monthly vs Annual.

- For Stripe subscription payments, add the **Payment Gateway** field to the form and ensure that **Stripe** is enabled.

- Then, in the form builder, go to **Fields → Payment Fields** and drag **Subscription Plan** into your form.

- Click the field to open its settings. By default it has 3 plan options — edit the label and price for each.

- To add more plans click the + button; to remove one click the x button.

- To pre-select a plan, click the circle next to that option.

- To add product images to each plan, turn on Use image choices and upload an image per plan.

### Add a trial period

You can let new subscribers try your service for free before their first charge.

- Click the Subscription Plan field to open its settings.

- Turn on Enable Trial Period.

- Set the length — days, weeks, months, or years.

### Add an expiry date

If your subscription should stop automatically on a specific date, turn on Enable Expiry Date and pick the date from the calendar.

### Send Extra Customer Details to Stripe

By default, Stripe receives the payment amount and email. You can also send the visitor’s name, phone number, address, and a transaction description. This makes it easier to identify payments in your Stripe Dashboard.

- Click on the Payment Gateway

- Go to **Gateways → Stripe **and click on the accordion.

- Use the dropdowns to match each Stripe field (Name, Description, Phone, Address) to the matching field on your form.

- Click Save.

### Map a tax number

- Add a Number field to your form and label it (e.g. VAT Number).

- Go to **Payments → Stripe**, enable Sync Fields with Stripe, and on the Tax Number row select the Number field you added.

- Click Save.

### Finishing Up

- Click **Save** in the top right of the form builder.

- Embed the form directly into a page:

- **Existing page** — open the page, paste the shortcode where you want the form to appear, and update the page.

- **New page** — create a new page, paste the shortcode, and publish it.

- Alternatively, copy the shortcode located beside the **Save** button, then add a **Shortcode** block to any page and paste the shortcode into that block.

### How to setup webhook for Stripe

- Copy your Stripe webhook endpoint URL:`https://your-site.com/?evf-stripe-webhook=1`

- Log in to your **Stripe Dashboard** and go to **Developers → Webhooks**.

- Click **Add endpoint** and paste the URL above into the **Endpoint URL** field.

- Under **Select events**, add the events below, then click **Add endpoint**.

- Stripe generates a **Signing secret** (it starts with `whsec_`). Click **Reveal** and copy it.

- In WordPress, go to **Everest Forms → Settings → Payments → Payment Method** and expand **Stripe Settings**. Paste the secret into the **Live Webhook Signing Secret** field (or **Test Webhook Signing Secret** if you’re in test mode).

- Save your settings.

Note: Use the Test signing secret while Test mode is enabled and the Live secret once you go live. The secret must match the mode, or Stripe's signature check will fail and the webhook is rejected.
